page: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by Microsoft's custom ARM implementation using Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz. It features 16 physical cores configured with one thread per core for a total of 16 dedicated vCPUs. The CPU cache layout includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is present via AES extensions, while x86 vector extensions and hyperthreading are absent by architectural design.

The instance includes 944 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed ephemeral capacity suitable for caching, temporary data, and swap operations alongside Premium Storage support. In benchmark testing, the memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput: PassMark memory ranks in the top tier (3241.27), backed by uncached large-block read bandwidth of 312.21 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 125.75 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression also registers in the upper 25% at 32.98 GB/sec.

General computational metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1683.0), multi-core (14755.0), and stress-ng tests, consistently score within the middle 50% average tier. Similarly, transactional workloads yield 32.55 million Redis SET operations per second, static web serving achieves 28.04 GB/sec, and PassMark database operations record 19651.76. LLM prompt processing on a medium 7B model falls into the bottom 25% (24.69 tokens/sec), reflecting the absence of discrete GPUs or specialized matrix instruction sets.

With its 1:4 compute-to-RAM balance, strong memory bus throughput, and bundled high-speed NVMe storage, the D16pds_v6 is well aligned for mid-tier enterprise workloads, caching layers, containerized microservices, build farms, and relational or document database systems that benefit from fast local temporary storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v6 is a general-purpose ARM64 virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated physical cores based on the Neoverse-N2 microarchitecture running at 3.4 GHz, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 944 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. It provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation alongside a 128 MB L3 cache and hardware AES encryption. Benchmark results indicate exceptional memory subsystem performance, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong uncached read bandwidth reaching 312.21 GB/sec. Standard processing metrics, including Geekbench and multi-threaded decompression, place in the middle tier, while matrix and heavy LLM inference tasks remain limited due to the lack of dedicated acceleration hardware. The inclusion of fast local NVMe storage and solid memory bandwidth makes this instance technically suited for database workloads, Redis caching, CI/CD compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
